description: App-level navigation: Application::Navigation -> Navigation::Menu -> Menu::FieldMapping -> Property{Type:Page} names the target page. A brand-new page exists but has NO menu entry until this chain is built.
notes: FieldMapping can be owned by a Menu directly (parent key "Menu", Name always "Page" for this use) — the same node shape reused a third way alongside Container- and Popup-owned FieldMapping.

Every Menu observed live carries an explicit scalar "Navigation" back-ref to its parent — CLAUDE.md separately notes that a NEW-style Menu carries this key while an old-style one may lack it; no old-style (Navigation-less) Menu was directly re-examined in this pass, so build new Menus WITH the key and treat a Menu missing it as merely legacy, not broken.

"Same view for all roles" is achieved by pointing every role's Navigation::Menu entries at the SAME Menu ids (sharing Menu/FieldMapping/Property nodes across Navigations) rather than duplicating them — Navigation nodes carry no role key themselves; the role->Navigation binding lives outside this draft entirely.

One Application can hold many Navigation sets (one conventionally per app-role, e.g. "Requester Navigation", "Admin Navigation") plus stray ad-hoc ones the builder UI creates on "Add page" if you are not careful which Navigation is currently selected — a page can exist and even have a Menu pointing at it while still never appearing in any role's actual nav, if that Menu landed in the wrong (or a brand-new, orphaned) Navigation.
